note: Outside the stated ICP on four of five criteria, and he closed at full price plus a 20% instalment uplift. He is a longshoreman who spent six years on supplemental status to reach a full-time slot, not a business owner or physician. On income he is the marginal case the ICP is meant to exclude: around $2,000 monthly disposable, no credit card, a credit score he describes as shot and is actively paying to repair, a $7,000 van repair in December and a $1,000-a-month obligation still running. Health is not a neglected area of an otherwise sorted life — he sustained a bilateral lumbar sprain at work a month ago and is in active chiropractic care, which is closer to injury management than to neglect. And the goal is explicitly preservation rather than good-to-great: 'at this point, I'm beyond aesthetics, just trying to preserve my health, my muscle strength, cardio, for the job.' He passes only the deconditioning exclusion — he is a manual labourer who trained through the second half of last year and has twice passed a physical agility test. Read alongside the Soneel Raj call the previous day, this is the clearest statement of the pattern in this batch: the one prospect who met the ICP on every criterion deferred, and the prospect who met one of five bought. If the buying population really does look like this, the stated ICP is not describing the customer, and — since it contains no clinical and no genuine affordability screen — it is also not protecting anyone.
